title: dev-onboard-survey survey.json: a deterministic first look at a codebase
description: Written by dev-onboard-survey (scripts/survey.py, no model) to <evid_root>/onboard/<project>/survey.json. It is the onboarding loop's orientation: what the repo is made of, the commands the repo itself declares, where execution starts, where the record lives, which files change most, and a first cut of areas sized for one reader each. Everything in it is counted or read from a file, never guessed, so two runs on the same commit write the same survey apart from timing. The how and why stages fan out over its areas; dev-onboard-map seeds the map's areas from it; the staleness check re-runs it. See docs/onboarding-loop.md.

commit.description: HEAD's full SHA when the repo is a git checkout, null otherwise. A map built from a null-commit survey cannot be refreshed incrementally.

source.description: git: the file list is `git ls-files`, so ignored files are already out. tree: a plain directory walk with the default excludes.

skipped.description: Files left out as binary, generated, vendored or too large to read.

languages.description: Code languages by line count, largest first.

manifests.description: Build and package manifests found (package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, Makefile, ...).

commands.description: Commands the repo itself declares, each with the file and line it was read from. Never invented: a command with source `convention` is the toolchain's documented default for a manifest that declares none (go test ./... for a go.mod).

name.description: The target or script name as declared.

run.description: How to invoke it, e.g. `make test` or `npm run lint`.

entry_points.description: Where execution starts, each with why the survey thinks so.

docs.description: Prose a newcomer should read: READMEs, docs/, contributing and architecture notes.

decisions.description: Decision records (ADRs, RFCs, docs/decisions). The why stage starts here.

hotspots.description: Files touched by the most commits in the recent history window, most first. Empty without git history.

shallow.description: True on a shallow clone: the why stage will find less of the record, and should say so.

areas.description: A first cut of the units to fan out over, each sized for one reader. Path-based and deterministic; dev-onboard-map may rename, merge or split them.

depends_on.description: Other area ids this one imports from, read from import statements where the survey can parse them (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript). Absent edges mean not detected, not absent.

tests.description: Test files whose name or imports point at this area.

notes.description: What the survey could not do and why, in plain words (no git, shallow history, an area too large to split).
